title: Cotechino with Lentils
summary: Italian tradition says lentils bring prosperity in the new year. The pairing is rich and satisfying, and a little cotechino goes a long way.

steps.text: Cook the cotechino according to the packet instructions (usually simmered in water for {timer:20-30|cotechino}). Keep warm.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook for {timer:8-10}, until very soft and golden.
Add the garlic and cook for {timer:1}. Add the rinsed lentils, bay leaves and stock, and bring to the boil.
Reduce to a simmer and cook for {timer:25-30|lentils}, until the lentils are tender but not mushy. Add water if it gets too dry.
Season well with salt and pepper, stir in the parsley and remove the bay leaves.
Slice the cotechino, allowing 125 g per person. Serve over the lentils, with polenta or mashed potatoes if you like.

tips: A standard cotechino weighs 500 g, which is 125 g per person. It is very rich, so this portion works well. The generous soffritto base adds volume and flavour. The dish tastes better made ahead, as the flavours meld overnight.
